newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA REDUCES MEAT IMPORT TAX.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA REDUCES MEAT IMPORT TAX.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Monday cut meat import duties in a bid to lower domestic retail prices, a government official said.

Under the decision, duties levied on imported meat will be reduced to three percent plus 170 European Currency Units per tonne, from a five percent import tax plus 244 Ecus per tonne, from July 1, Trade Minister Valentin Vassilev told reporters.
"This measure aims to counteract attempts by some business groups which have monopolised the local meat market to racketeer the consumers with unjustifiably high prices," said Vassilev.
The duty cut is part of government measures to free basic food prices in line with preparations to launch a restrictive monetary regime known as a currency board on July 1.
